podcast.body: A single from the 1997 album "Earthling," which gained significant attention when Trent Reznor collaborated with Bowie on a remix. This collaboration excited fans who saw Bowie's mid-90s experiments leaning towards industrial rock. "On a remix of Bowie's single I'm Afraid of Americans from his 1997 album Earthling."

podcast.body: From the album "Earthling," this song featured a Nine Inch Nails remix and an accompanying music video that starred Trent Reznor in a "creepy stalker" role, visually compared to the film "Taxi Driver." Bowie also toured with Trent Reznor during this period. "Bowie and a 9-inch nails remix of I'm Afraid of Americans, originally from the 1997 album Earthling."

podcast.body: This single was a collaboration between David Bowie and Trent Reznor and was featured on Bowie's 1997 album, *Earthling*. The song was part of Bowie's exploration into new genres of dance music during that period. "We touched on this record last time with his collaboration with Trent Rezner on the single I'm Afraid of Americans."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This song from the "Earthling" album had a creepy stalker music video that featured Trent Reznor of Nine Inch Nails, a diehard Bowie fan. The video's style was compared to Martin Scorsese's "Taxi Driver" and gained plenty of attention. "Not only did they tour together, but Bowie got Trent to appear in the creepy stalker video for this song from 1997 called I'm Afraid of Americans, which looks like something straight out of Martin Scorsese Taxi Driver."
